SHAPE DOES NOT PREDICT THE ANSWER, and this is the census's main caution. game/sys/memcard classifies `top_of_file` -- its opener does sit above the first function definition and covers all 30 compiled functions -- yet it was dispatched TWICE as a lost-closer bug purely on the strength of 'an off with no reset', and it is load-bearing (attempt.MC_memcard-pragma-leak-is-load-bearing-reproduced.20260904.v1). Read the shape column as a prior, never as a verdict.

BOTH BARE-RESET READINGS ARE REPORTED, as al_pragma_extent reports both presence and extent. Under the leak law (a bare `#pragma reset` closes nothing) the count is 37 regions in 36 files; under `--bare-closes-all` it is 36 in 35. Exactly ONE region turns on that assumption, in game/enemy/enemy, which holds the image's only bare `#pragma reset`.

PARSER CALIBRATION, TWO-SIDED, against fndiff.raw_signature's roster for the 36 census units that have a built object -- 970 real functions: mc_pragma_regions false-positive 60, missed 63; al_pragma_extent false-positive 97, missed 73. The residual splits into two classes, neither harmful in the same way: (a) static helpers present in the source but INLINED or dead-stripped, so absent from the object yet genuinely inside the region -- most of the 60; and (b) ONE file, game/movie/movieplayer, where an `extern "C" {` block wrapping the TU means brace depth never returns to zero and NOTHING parses, which is 52 of the 63 misses on its own. Class (b) is the dangerous direction because an unparsed file reports `covered 0` and reads as 'no functions affected', so those rows print PARSE-FAIL rather than a zero. On the single unit with an independent ground-truth roster (game/sys/memcard, defake_gate baseline) the parser is exact: 30 parsed, 30 covered, 30 real, zero either way.

A COVERAGE COUNT PUBLISHED IN THIS AREA HAS BEEN WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE. The figure '33 of 35 functions', which appears in attempt.AL_optpropagation-coverage-does-not-predict-the-addr16lo-class-and-the-presence-screen-manufactures-the-separation.20260904.v1, in al_pragma_extent's printed output, and in run 54's memcard work order, is produced by al_pragma_extent.scan_functions, which identifies a definition as 'the last identifier before the ( of a brace block'. That also matches control flow and multi-line macros: on memcard.c it returns 35 heads, of which TWO are the same `while` (a do-while at src/game/sys/memcard.c:1046 and its tail at :1068) and two are `#define` bodies (CARD_RETRY_PROMPT, and mb_blit's SIH_OFF is the same shape). The tool then stores coverage in a dict keyed by name, so the duplicate `while` silently collapses on the covered side but not on the parsed side -- the 33 and the 35 are not taken over the same population. The true figure is 30 of 30: the region covers every compiled function in the TU. Both halves of the error pointed the same way, at a region that looked like it spared two functions and spares none.
